semanticDecisions: an atom compares in place only when the widths agree (Latin-1 atom vs Latin-1 value, native-order UTF-16 atom vs UTF-16 value); every other shape folds windows, so results never depend on the layout

local width-2 atoms are written in the host byte order; the per-atom flag stays and every reader follows it, so mapped lexicon atoms (recorded big-endian) and foreign-order atoms keep working through copySwapMemory/reverseBytes
bulk copies start at 64 units: copyMemory is a runtime call whose fixed cost loses below that (bench 32 vs 256)
admission keeps its validating per-unit hash loops: the structural mix hash dominates admission and bulk writes with temporary arrays measured slower on short inputs
the Latin-1 getChars loop stays as it was: C2 vectorizes it, an eight-units-per-load unpack measured slower
